proof_summary: Letting \(d=D(n)\), when \(d\mid n\) appending a zero gives the partner \(10n\). Otherwise congruence of a number with its digit sum modulo \(9\) makes \(a=(n-D(d))/9\) integral; after establishing \(d<10^a\), the construction \(k=d(10^a-1)10^{a+\ell(d)}+d\) satisfies \(d\mid k\), and the decimal-complement identity \(D(10^a-d)+D(d-1)=9a\) gives \(D(k)=D(d)+9a=n\), while \(k\ne n\) follows from \(d\nmid n\).
